llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Instruction requires page numbers to be 'positioned at the center', but the metric function has_page_numbers_in_footers (docs.py:594-612) does NOT check footer alignment or centering at all
Weak verification logic: The metric only checks 'if not any(char.isdigit() for char in footer_text)' which is too simplistic - any digit in footer passes (e.g., 'Version 1' would incorrectly pass)
Limited scope: Metric only checks footer.paragraphs[0].text - if page numbers are in a different paragraph, they won't be detected
Missing page coverage verification: The function checks sections have footers with digits, but doesn't properly verify that page numbers actually appear on every page as required
Function signature issue: has_page_numbers_in_footers only takes one parameter (docx_file) but should follow standard metric signature (result, expected)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add alignment/centering check: Use paragraph.paragraph_format.alignment to verify footer paragraphs are center-aligned (WD_PARAGRAPH_ALIGNMENT.CENTER)
Strengthen page number detection: Use python-docx field detection to check for actual PAGE field in footer, not just any digit
Check all footer paragraphs: Iterate through all footer.paragraphs, not just the first one
Verify page coverage: Check footer content across all sections to ensure page numbers are present throughout the document
Fix function signature: Update metric to accept (result, expected) parameters to match OSWorld conventions
